issues.description: Method signature mismatch for SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery. The problem statement (UML and textual description) declares acceptSupplyDelivery as acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) — i.e., four parameters including a supplier name (see UML and text). The provided code examples and the solution implement a three-parameter method acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) where the first String is the ingredient name (no supplierName parameter). This inconsistency leaves students unsure which signature to implement and may cause compilation/runtime mismatches (implementing the 4-parameter variant per the UML will not match the 3-parameter calls present in Main/solution or vice versa).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across all artifacts. Option A (recommended given existing code examples): update the problem statement UML and textual description to declare acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (three parameters) to match the template Main and the solution implementation. Option B: change the template and solution implementation (and all calls in Main) to acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update examples in the problem text/UML accordingly. Apply the chosen signature everywhere (problem text, UML, example Main, and SealSaloon implementation) to avoid confusion and compilation mismatches.
